title: Objects and Structures
summary: Objects (or structs/classes instances) bundle related data and behavior: a "User" might have name, email, and methods like login().
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Objects (or structs/classes instances) bundle related data and behavior: a "User" might have name, email, and methods like login().
This is the bridge from raw data to modeling the real world. Even simple programs benefit — a point has x and y; an invoice has lines and a total.
Key points: group fields that belong together, methods keep data and logic in one place, and start simple — you do not need full OOP for small scripts.

sections.codeExample:
user = { name: "Alice", age: 30 }
// an object groups related fields under one name

sections.content: Summary: Objects and Structures — practice the example by changing values and predicting the output before running it.
